chapter: Chris Kelly and the country bands
title: Chris Kelly: knowing him in the country, his cornet and Kelly's Blues
summary: Kelly was much older; he played a short cornet with mute and plunger, famously drawing a crowd with a blues played from the dance hall window.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: Had you known Chris Kelly down in the country? Oh yeah. You knew him down there before you moved up? Oh yeah. Yeah Chris was a little bit of big under Chris. And he was bigger than, a good deal older then? Oh yeah he was way older.

Oh yeah he was way older than me. Yeah I remember him used to play. You know. I always say I wanted to be a musician. I used to follow him everywhere until I got big enough to learn how to play you see.

Had you heard him down in the country playing there? Oh lots of time. Lots of time. Since he's dead now we can't ask him anything. No. So we have to find out from his friends and people like you that heard him. That's right. That's right.

Now he was a wonderful trumpet player but he would never use a trumpet. He always used a short cornet. Short cornet. And uh, Kellis Love Blues. Yes. He was the only one I used to love to hear play. He was the only one who could play the Kellis Love Blues. He was really great on that first. Yeah he was the only one. The only one I would have heard playing around. Yeah. That's why I said he should have made some money on that. What style did he play? A Kellis Love? Yes. I mean did he use mute much or what the? That's right. He used one of them mutes. And one of those uh, flushes. You flush the. Oh yeah. Yeah. The rubber plunger. That's right. He used one of them. That's right. He used to use one of them. You put the mute in the horn first and then the plunger on top. That's right. Like that. That's right. And he used to be in the dance hall. Right there in Algy. He used to play at the young friends hall. Yeah. And he used to stick that little short cornet out the window. See around about eight o'clock they wouldn't have nobody in the hall. Around about ten o'clock they wouldn't have nobody. And he used to get to the window. And he put that cornet out the window. He started playing that Kellis Love Blues. And he take that uh, Splunger and put it over there. And about maybe about twenty minutes that the hall would be packing down with people. Oh man. That's right. He used to bring me in there. He could play the Kellis Love Blues. They'd have a big tone. You could hear him all over the neighborhood. Oh yeah. He had a sweet tone. He really had a wonderful tonation. Yeah. Sweet trumpet. Do you remember any of the other blues or anything he played? Well uh, he made another blues. I can't think of it. But the name of it was uh, Begunna Street Ich. Begunna Street Ich? Ich, yeah. He made that. But he never did put it on a record. He never made any records. No, he never made any records.
